samples.summary: New `seg()` guard is bypassed by the workspace identifier, which is still interpolated raw into every URL
samples.evidence: The change adds `seg()` for "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:21-32), but `HttpClient.base` (line 98) builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` with no encoding, and `listApiKeys` (397), `createApiKey` (404) and `revokeApiKey` (415) do the same for the management routes. `config.workspace` reaches the client straight from argv (`--workspace`, root.ts:66) or env/config file, so a value like `../../admin` or `ws-1?x=` retargets the same credentialed request the diff set out to protect — the exact failure mode described in the new doc comment, one segment earlier. `printDryRun` (dry-run.ts:30) interpolates it raw too, so the preview mirrors the mis-targeted URL rather than flagging it. The unit test only covers doc/tab/cell/key ids, not the workspace.

samples.summary: Import `--dry-run` previews still print unencoded document ids, so the preview no longer matches the request the client now sends
samples.evidence: `docs/import.ts:155` prints `path: `/documents/${replace}/content``, and `notes/import.ts:147` and `slides/import.ts:182` do the same. The live path for those commands is `putDocContent`/`putNoteContent`/`putSlidesContent`, which after this change encode the id via `seg()` (http-client.ts:297/303/331). The stated invariant of the change — "every identifier interpolated into a preview path goes through this" (dry-run.ts:4-11) — is therefore violated at three call sites the diff did not touch: `wafflebase docs import f.docx --replace 'a/b' --dry-run` prints `/documents/a/b/content` while the real run sends `/documents/a%2Fb/content`. Grepped `packages/cli/src` for `${docId}`/`${replace}`/`/documents/$` and reviewed every `printDryRun` call site; these three are the remaining unencoded preview paths.

samples.summary: `cells get --dry-run` re-implements the live endpoint-selection ternary, so the two can silently drift
samples.evidence: Lines 25-29 duplicate the `range?.includes(':') ? getCells : range ? getCell : getCells` decision made independently at lines 35-39. They agree today, but any future change to the selection rule (e.g. accepting a bare `A1:` or a named range) must be made twice or the preview will print an endpoint the command would not call — the one thing a dry run is supposed to guarantee.

finding.summary: New `seg()` guard is bypassed by the workspace identifier, which is still interpolated raw into every URL
finding.evidence: The change adds `seg()` for "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:21-32), but `HttpClient.base` (line 98) builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` with no encoding, and `listApiKeys` (397), `createApiKey` (404) and `revokeApiKey` (415) do the same for the management routes. `config.workspace` reaches the client straight from argv (`--workspace`, root.ts:66) or env/config file, so a value like `../../admin` or `ws-1?x=` retargets the same credentialed request the diff set out to protect — the exact failure mode described in the new doc comment, one segment earlier. `printDryRun` (dry-run.ts:30) interpolates it raw too, so the preview mirrors the mis-targeted URL rather than flagging it. The unit test only covers doc/tab/cell/key ids, not the workspace.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `seg()` (http-client.ts:30-32) documents that "Every interpolated identifier goes through this" to stop dot-segment/`?` retargeting, but `HttpClient.base` (http-client.ts:96-99) interpolates `this.config.workspace` unencoded ahead of every encoded segment, and `listApiKeys` (397), `createApiKey` (404) and `revokeApiKey` (415) do the same — line 415 even encodes `seg(id)` in the same template while leaving the workspace raw. `config.workspace` is unvalidated input on all four resolution branches of `resolveConfig` (config/config.ts:96-100, 121-126, 143-147, 160-164), fed straight from `--workspace <id>` (root.ts:66) via getConfig/getClient (root.ts:29-40), env, session or profile YAML. `printDryRun` (dry-run.ts:28-33) also interpolates it raw, so the preview mirrors the mis-targeted URL rather than flagging it, defeating the stated purpose of its own `seg()` (dry-run.ts:12-14). I found no validation or normalization of the workspace string anywhere in packages/cli/src, and http-client-paths.test.ts pins workspace to 'ws-1' (line 17) so no test covers it. The unencoded leading segment makes every downstream `seg()` moot, and a benign workspace containing a space/`?`/`#` yields a malformed or truncated request path — a real wrong-target/guard-completeness bug in the correctness lane, not solely a security concern.

searchedFor: Grep 'dryRun' in packages/cli/src (no hits in commands/api-keys.ts)
finding.summary: `api-keys revoke`/`create` still ignore `--dry-run` and execute the mutation
finding.evidence: This change adds `opts.dryRun` short-circuits to read commands, but `registerApiKeysCommand` has no `dryRun` check at all: `api-keys create <name>` (api-keys.ts:17 → `createApiKey`) and `api-keys revoke <key-id>` (api-keys.ts:45 → `revokeApiKey`, a DELETE) run the real request under `--dry-run`. A user (or agent) previewing `wafflebase api-keys revoke k-1 --dry-run` irreversibly revokes the key, even though the global flag is documented as 'Show request without executing' (root.ts:75) and docs/design/cli.md advertises dry-run as a first-class agent affordance. A grep for `dryRun` across packages/cli/src returns zero hits in api-keys.ts.

verdict.reason: The claim that registerApiKeysCommand "has no dryRun check at all" is false in the working tree. `api-keys create` short-circuits on opts.dryRun at packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:34-37, returning after printDryRunUrl(apiKeysUrl(opts), 'POST', { name }) and BEFORE createApiKey(name) on line 38. `api-keys revoke` short-circuits at :72-75, returning after printDryRunUrl(apiKeysUrl(opts, keyId), 'DELETE') and BEFORE revokeApiKey(keyId) on line 76, with an explicit comment at :70-71 noting revocation is irreversible. The file imports printDryRunUrl at :4 — a variant helper used because these API-key routes do not hang off the v1 API base that printDryRun builds (comment at :7-12) — so a search for the more common printDryRun helper would miss it. A grep for 'dryRun' in this file returns hits at lines 4, 32, 34, 52, 72, directly contradicting the claimed "zero hits in api-keys.ts". Regression tests assert the mutations are never issued under --dry-run: packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts:231-241 (expect(createApiKey).not.toHaveBeenCalled()) and :243-252 (expect(revokeApiKey).not.toHaveBeenCalled()). The reviewer's cited call-site lines (17 and 45) do not match the file: line 17 is the URL builder's return and line 45 is blank.

searchedFor: Grep 'dryRun' across packages/cli/src to enumerate commands with/without the guard
Read packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts, slides.ts (lines 20-150), files.ts in full
finding.summary: The same `--dry-run`-still-fetches bug is left unfixed in notes/slides/files read commands
finding.evidence: The change fixes `docs list`, `docs get`, `tabs list` and `cells get`, but identical read commands elsewhere still hit the network under `--dry-run`: `notes get` (notes.ts:76 `getDocument`), `notes list` (notes.ts:35 `listDocuments`), `slides get` (slides.ts:81), `slides list` (slides.ts:40), `files list` (files.ts:85) and `files get` (files.ts:105). Each of these has no `opts.dryRun` branch, so `--dry-run` performs the very request it promises not to send — the same behavior this PR describes as a bug (burnt rate limit, access-log entry). The fix is partial and leaves the flag's semantics inconsistent across sibling namespaces.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `notes get/list`, `slides get/list` and `files list/get` lack an `opts.dryRun` branch and therefore hit the network under `--dry-run`. Every one of the six cited commands in fact contains an early-return dry-run guard placed before the client call. notes.ts:35-40 guards `listDocuments()` (line 41); notes.ts:82-85 guards `getDocument()` (line 86); slides.ts:40-45 guards `listDocuments()` (line 46); slides.ts:87-90 guards `getDocument()` (line 91); files.ts:87-92 guards `listDocuments()` (line 93); files.ts:113-116 guards `getDocument()` (line 117). Each branch calls `printDryRun(...)` then `return`, so no request is issued. The reviewer's line numbers point at the `.command(...)` registration or the client call rather than the action body, which likely explains the miss. The guard is reachable: the global flag is declared at root.ts:75 (`.option('--dry-run', ...)`) and typed at root.ts:21 (`dryRun: boolean`), and `getGlobalOpts` supplies it. The pattern is applied consistently across the sibling namespaces as well (create/rename/delete/content/export in notes.ts and slides.ts, download/rename/delete in files.ts, and `dryRun: opts.dryRun` threaded into the import/upload helpers), so the claimed inconsistency does not exist either.
